build: Software Projects disk, alternate D64 with LA–LJ files

exclude: Disk staging for bytes copied to $1E00 and graphics decoded to $4000; disk tail remains in the queue.
extra: Scene bytes copied by the runtime loader
Tail of the file loaded at $8010, role unresolved

comments.text: The first copied byte in the scene record is $03. The caller starts executing one byte later.
Save and reload the caller stack pointer, copy the score digits, set up screen and colour pointers, use sound request $87 and initialize expanded sprite 1 before applying the scene colour lookup.
Restore the saved stack pointer, copy the digit characters and initialize score pointers. Select the room sprite configuration and start sound $87 before switching the VIC bank.
Set sprite 1 to X=$9F and Y=$34. Expand it in both directions, put it behind the background and select its colour 7 before applying the room colour table.

Select pose 5 and install projectile preset 3. Set signed projectile velocities to 4 and -12, then advance sprite 2 in a ten-iteration input window. A matching direction enters the next sequence, while exhaustion takes the retry jump.
Call the score service and request sound $87. Alternate pose changes and sprite movement, including two leftward character shifts in the right wall strip, before polling the next input.
Load pose records 9 and 10 with weapon shapes 5 and 0. Advance to successive pose and shape pairs with timed updates between them.
Move the pose across the screen, call the score service and request sound $87. Begin the next projectile update window with counter 9.
Install pose 9 and weapon shape 5, call the score service and request sound $86. Step through three further pose selections and initialize sprite 2 with frame $C0 at coordinates $9D,$9D.
Call the score service, request sound $87 and install the raster handler at $2D95. Select the character matrix with $D018=$0F, then apply successive overlay records to sprites 4–7.
Call the score service, select overlay records $0E and $0F with movement updates between them, then leave sprite 1 enabled. Decrement $25 and restore the saved stack pointer before returning.
Read port 2, invert the active-low bits, compare the result to the previous sample in $28 and store the new sample there without changing the comparison flags.
Use A as the iteration count. Advance the projectile, clearing its vertical movement gate when sprite 1 reaches X=$9A, and call the sprite-follow routine.
When sprite 1 has low X below $C0, copy the X and Y registers of sprite 2 into sprite 1.
Double A and read the selected jump address from $292C. The entries start at different points of the cascading matrix-clear sequence.
Clear four cells in each of three screen rows beginning at $4175, $419D and $41C5, then continue to the smaller clears.
Clear twelve five-cell rows starting at $40F1 through $293F, then fall through to the two remaining matrix clears.
Clear five cells in both $4182 and $41AA rows, then clear the four fixed cells.
Write character zero to matrix cells $4171, $4172, $4199 and $419A.

Save the expected action in $10 and read the joystick with active-low bits inverted. Return the expected mask on an exact match. No input returns $FF. An incorrect nonzero mask also requests sound $89 and starts a 20-call cooldown.
Four little-endian addresses selected by A at $28BE. Later entries in the routine skip the initial clears and fall through to the smaller patches.
Cooldown decremented by the action matcher at $28FC. A wrong direction reloads it to $14.
Clear five character cells on each of twelve rows from $4112. Advance the pointer by 40 per row.
Set up the same twelve-row clear from $40F1 and fall through into its shared loop.
Read the first colour at $D912, add one and write the same result to a five-column by twelve-row strip.
Select $D8F1 as the starting colour cell and fall through to the common strip update.
Move nine characters one cell right on each of 23 rows starting at $4050 and clear the first cell. Reapply the colour lookup in page $46.
Move nine characters one cell left on each of 23 rows starting at $406E and clear the last cell. Reapply the colour lookup in page $46.
Update sprite 2 on expiry of $31A4. Add the two velocity bytes, toggle the high X bit on a low-byte wrap and change its vertical behaviour at the $E0 threshold.
The common return from the horizontal velocity adjustment and the lower screen cutoff at $2A79.
Request sound $8A and increment the colour of sprite 2 sixteen times with timed updates between increments. Set the last colour to $0D.
Select pose 8 and fall through to the common retry delay.
Request sound $89, wait using the timed update with A=$28, call $0ECD and jump to the initialization at $1E04.
Use A to index sprite 2 frame, coordinate and high-X tables. Initialize its colour to zero and enable the sprite.
Repeat the timed joystick and sprite updates using the initial count in A. Update the weapon-room animation on each iteration.
Wait through two CIA2 timer intervals, poll the joystick and apply the sprite cycle update. Repeat with the count in A saved to $2EC6.
Every three calls advance $31A2 down through 2, 1, 0 and write pointer $BA plus that index to sprite 1.
Use the shared 90-byte record index at $3200. Wait for the lower raster and copy the record to the zero-page sprite work area.
Multiply A by eighteen and add $304C. Load positions, colours and frame pointers for sprites 4–7. Replace the upper nibbles of the VIC expansion masks with the final two fields.

Use A to select sprite 0 coordinates, expansion masks and a source pointer. Select frame $A9. The source begins with the number of zero bytes to emit, followed by literal bytes that complete the 64-byte frame at $6A40.
Reset the band index and select the bank and character matrix. Schedule $2C58 at the line in $99 and apply the first group of coordinates, colours and frame pointers to sprites 5–7.
Set the next interrupt to $2C98 at the line in $9A. Use the second group of coordinates, colours and frame pointers for sprites 5–7.
Set the next interrupt to $2CD8 at the line in $9B. Use the third group of coordinates, colours and frame pointers for sprites 5–7.
Set the next interrupt to $2D18 at the line in $9C. Use the fourth group of coordinates, colours and frame pointers for sprites 5–7.
Set the next interrupt to $2D58 at the line in $9D. Use the fifth group of coordinates, colours and frame pointers for sprites 5–7.
Set the next interrupt to $2C07 at raster line 1. Use the sixth group of coordinates, colours and frame pointers for sprites 5–7.
Service the resident sound and tape port at $1783 and jump to the shared IRQ return.
Advance the band index, schedule $2C07 at raster line 1 and select VIC bank $0000 with $D018=$15 before returning through the IRQ epilogue.
When the index at $316D reaches six, clear it and the active flag, then store character 1 at the saved cell pointer and colour $0C at its companion colour address.

Decrement the divider at $316C. At zero advance the index at $316D and reload the divider to seven. Use the index loaded before the increment to select a character from $317F, then set its cell colour to 1.
Use A times two to select the screen cell pointer from $316F, then initialize the character index to zero and divider to one. Decrement the activity byte at $316E.
Wait through the shared raster synchronization and put the six-band handler entry $2C07 in $42/$43.
Use source $7400 and destination $4000, then fall through to the matrix copy and colour update.
Use source $4000 and destination $0400. Share the copy loop, which skips the eight sprite pointer positions before applying the colour lookup in page $46.
Use A as a movement count. Increase the three low X coordinates in each of the six pose bands and move sprite 0 right, setting its high X on wrap.
Use A as a movement count. Decrease the three low X coordinates in each of the six pose bands and the low X of sprite 0.
Pass three consecutive sprite indices $CB through $CD to the shared sprite transform at $16AD.
An authored zero slot between the mirror routine return and the weapon sequence countdown.
Countdown set before the Weapons Room movement and input sequences. The timed update at $2B03 also uses it.
Set to 16 at $2A92 and decremented between sprite 2 colour increments.
Zero slot between the flash countdown at $2EC7 and the wait countdown at $2EC9.
Iteration counter used by the sprite follow loop and the timed wait at $2AF2.
Two zero bytes before the six packed shape pointers at $2ECC. The shape pointer index uses $2ECC as its base.
Nineteen little-endian pointers selected by twice the shape index in the sprite 0 builder at $2BDF.
Nineteen pairs of low X and Y coordinates loaded into sprite 0 by the shape builder.
One sprite 0 horizontal expansion bit per shape index, merged into $D01D.
One sprite 0 vertical expansion bit per shape index, merged into $D017.
Packed sprite 0 frame. The first byte requests 35 zero bytes. The following 29 source bytes, through $2F5B, complete the frame at $6A40.
Packed sprite 0 frame. The first byte requests 39 zero bytes. The following 25 source bytes, through $2F74, complete the frame at $6A40.
Packed sprite 0 frame. The first byte requests 35 zero bytes. The following 29 source bytes, through $2F91, complete the frame at $6A40.
Packed sprite 0 frame. The first byte requests 60 zero bytes. The following 4 source bytes, through $2F95, complete the frame at $6A40.
Packed sprite 0 frame. The first byte requests 23 zero bytes. The following 41 source bytes, through $2FBE, complete the frame at $6A40.
Packed sprite 0 frame. The first byte requests 45 zero bytes. The following 19 source bytes, through $2FD1, complete the frame at $6A40.
Packed sprite 0 frame. The first byte requests 37 zero bytes. The following 27 source bytes, through $2FEC, complete the frame at $6A40.
Packed sprite 0 frame. The first byte requests 57 zero bytes. The following 7 source bytes, through $2FF3, complete the frame at $6A40.
Packed sprite 0 frame. The first byte requests 15 zero bytes. The following 49 source bytes, through $3024, complete the frame at $6A40.
Packed sprite 0 frame. The first byte requests 24 zero bytes. The following 40 source bytes, through $304C, complete the frame at $6A40.
Sixteen 18-byte records selected by the loader at $2B56. Each holds eight position bytes, four sprite colours, four frame pointers and the two expansion masks for sprites 4–7.
Divider, current character index and activity flag for the cell animation at $2DBB–$2E18.
Eight screen cell address pairs available to the selector at $2DFF.
Five consecutive character codes indexed by the cell animation at $2DEA.
Reset in the first raster handler and incremented by subsequent handlers.
Seven frame pointers available to the sprite 2 preset selector.
Seven pairs of low X and Y coordinates available to the sprite 2 preset selector.
Seven high X masks merged into bit 2 of $D010 when a projectile preset is selected.
Two counters decremented and reloaded by $2B15.

Projectile initialization record. The update at $2A21 reads the divider reload, divider, X and Y velocities, X and Y adjustments and the threshold at $31A9. The scene also writes $31AA with its presets.

Seven six-character rows for the Weapons Room sequence at $26DE. The first row copies columns 0–4. The next six copy columns 0–5. Destination rows start at $41CF with zero written to the corresponding colour cells.
This scene record ends with the eleven byte marker copied by the unpacker at $0DDE.
The first page of the screen matrix for the background in VIC bank $4000. Its character codes index the scene colour lookup when the display is initialized.
Screen matrix offsets $100–$1FF. The VIC reads these as character codes and the palette routine processes a page at a time.
Screen matrix offsets $200–$2FF. The screen maps into the glyph data at $7800.
The last page of the screen matrix, including the hardware sprite pointers at $43F8–$43FF.
The two sprite fragments before the active player pair at $4480.
Two 64-byte sprite images for hardware sprites 5 and 6 at the Weapons Room capture.
Four individual sprite shapes between the active player pair and the colour table.
Table indexed by the room screen cells when the scene patches $167A to $46 and calls the shared colour routine.
Sixteen 64-byte rendered fragments including torso, hand and bent-leg graphics.
Animation parts with compact head and foot shapes in the low slots and angled limbs in the high slots.
Sixteen mask fragments immediately before the row of compact leaning poses.
Middle mask set for the player animation with varied angles of legs and armour.
Another set of adjacent sprite fragments showing outlines of boots and legs.
Sprite parts in the $6C–$7B pointer range, including the separate pair of straight lower legs.
Sixty-four-byte sprite pieces for mixed arm, head, and body animation frames.
Rendered bank of fragments continuing the player motion set, including pointed foot and knee shapes.
The 16 sprite records around the pointer $A9 selected for sprite 0 in the later room routine.
Upper range of sprite masks before the expanded sprite, including a circular weapon silhouette at pointer $B8.
The 64-byte image record selected by sprite 1 at the Weapons Room capture. Both expansion bits are set during initialization.
Seven 64-byte slots with separate shapes such as a circular disk, star and fragments of weapons. The code writes pointer $C0 to sprite 2.
The unpacked picture stream initializes $7100–$73FF to zero. These bytes are still zero in the play capture.
Character template for the background copy at $2E25. The destination is the active matrix at $4000, with the eight sprite pointer bytes preserved.
The scene character glyph store for VIC bank $4000 and character-base bits 3–1 of $D018 set to 7. A character occupies eight consecutive bytes.
The top half of this scene set, from character code $80. The eight-byte glyph slots are used for the scene-specific objects and screen details.
The LC bytes at $B612–$B616 follow the last source token required by the scene picture decoder and precede the repeated disk fill.
Repeated $04 bytes at $B617–$B70F, after the input consumed by the scene picture decode.
